page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword or signature.

main_text.p: Blificabitis[?] adhuc in senectute, nec resilietis ad Hostium conspectum in porta. Vnicum addo, & finio. Rubus dixit aliquando Hortulano, si mihi esset quispiam, qui curam mei gereret, plantaret, irrigaret & coleret (quod effusè fit caeteris plantis & arboribus) Reges profectò me desiderarent, & aspicerent florem meum & fructus[?] Vnde accepit eum Hortulanus, plantavit, in horti medio, in optimo Terrae, irrigavit eum: Sed quid inde fit? Invaluerunt praeter spem & votum ipsius spinae, germina & rami supra omnes arbores, quae circum ipsum erant, & operierunt folia ejus terram, & impletus est hortus ab eo, & multitudine spinarum, & nemo potuit tutò ad ipsum accedere. Hactenus Locmannus Arabicè Mythologus, simile quiddam de Rhamno Cedris Libani, minitantis incendium, suppeditat Textus sacer Iudicum. 9. Ingeniosos alloquor; Non necesse est igitur, ut prolixius explicem. Adducti estis vos (Baccalaurei) in saltum melleum, deterreat vos (oro) juramentum, ne manus ori il-

page.notes: Left edge of the scan is darkened by a binding shadow, so the first letter of the first word ("Blificabitis") is doubtful; it is probably "Ædificabitis" or similar and is marked [?]. The last line is cut off by the bottom edge of the scan after "il-", so the rest of the word is not visible and is not transcribed. "fructus" in the phrase "aspicerent florem meum & fructus" is hard to read and is marked [?]. The page number "43" is clear. Italic and roman type were judged from the scan and may contain small errors.
